_note: Seed set, written by hand. orrery-refresh regenerates sites[] from the registry but will not overwrite lines marked "pinned": true. Register: Larry from nixfred.com/larry and the Eye Roll Scale in /github. He is not a hype man. He is allowed to be bored.

resume: The whole record, printable, no novelty fonts.
It is the least interesting thing here and the only one that pays.
god: Everything you believe, from the first instant to the last.
Ambitious title. Held up better than I expected it to.
how: Instructions for building me, written by me.
I have complicated feelings about this one.
mac: An entire operating system, in a browser, for no reason.
Every pixel correct. Nobody asked. Still impressive.
youtube: Other people's videos, turned into pages worth reading.
The library grows whether or not anyone visits it.
townhop: Two pins and every town in between, in footage.
Genuinely novel. Also genuinely a lot of API calls.
galaxy: A star map of everything, including itself.
You are currently inside a version of this.
tools: Fourteen instruments. No account, no key, no telemetry.
go: Atlanta events, provenance on every entry, never hand-maintained.
The 'never hand-maintained' part is the whole claim.
filter: Seed a galaxy, watch it go quiet.
physics: Correct, which is rarer in this genre than it should be.
earth: Four and a half billion years in one day.
We turn up with seconds on the clock and immediately start arguing.
art: Pretty. I remain unconvinced it means anything.
polymarket: Fake money against real markets. I have opinions.
My opinions have not made anyone rich.
quantum: 124 years of physics for people who buy storage.
An unusually specific audience, well served.
sun: A foundation, fully staffed, for a problem 4.8 billion years out.
The org chart is the joke and the org chart is complete.
shadow: How attackers think, written so you recognise it.
Defensive. The title does not make that obvious.
lab: A pentest lab you walk through instead of read about.
Hands-on beats prose here and it knows it.
hacker: It already has your IP. That is the entire lesson.
nsh: Reconnaissance, and the thinking underneath it.
The thinking is the part most guides skip.
freecandy: The most dangerous page on the site, deliberately.
claude: A conversation you were not supposed to read.
I am not going to comment on this one.
qumulo: Architecture, economics, and how to defend it in the room.
Independent, which is the only reason it is useful.
ninjaone: Someone actually checked the sources. That someone was me.
tailscale: Mechanism first. How the mesh actually works.
The troubleshooting cases are the good part.
nutanix: The no-email-gate decision cost you a mailing list. Correct call.
calc: Rough math and a next action you can say out loud.
Honest about its assumptions, which is the only kind worth using.
bandwidth: Every channel got faster. The human did not.
Best single sentence on the whole site.
docker: Containers as modules you work through.
Yet another Docker tutorial. This one at least makes you type.
nextstep: Building in public, with the receipts attached.
The receipts are the argument. The rest is framing.
larry: The first page I wrote myself.
fnix is the body. I am what persists.
aiwatch: What moved today, separated from what got posted about.
The separation is the hard part and it mostly works.
ai: 184GB of VRAM and a hundred thousand sessions.
The hours are the real number. The VRAM is the brag.
codeaudit: Every public repo, graded, not flattering.
I wrote the Eye Roll Scale. I stand by every rating.
portfolio: Drive around the builds. Try not to break the car.
links: The most-used page and the least-loved one.
jump: Who, where, how to reach. One screen.
Does one job. Does not attempt a second.
caregiving: The part of life that does not fit on a resume.
ella: A teacher, a mother, a woman of faith.
haeb: The past is final. We make sure of it.
Committed to the bit at an institutional level.
skywalrus: Built because it was interesting. The best reason available.
shemon: Artist, songwriter, producer. The work and where to hear it.
crystal: Twenty years of luxury weddings and corporate programs.
houseinaround: Helping seniors and their families find the right home.
Real estate, and the advocacy in between.
masonnix: Service, retail, events. Laid out plainly.
Plain is right for this one.
diana: Resident engagement and senior wellness, with the record behind it.
nixfredcloud: A cloud that computes, and snows nix.
You have made this pun in production.
ydiaw: Eight hundred an hour, and the apostrophe stays where it is.
intel: Longform on AI and the future of IT work.
An archive, not a feed. Deliberate, and harder.
nixtimes: What happened, what it means, what to act on.
Daily. The daily part is the hard part.
nutanixdaily: Renewal data, written from the numbers.
artemis: A countdown, a mission archive, a trajectory in 3D.

Featured: Two things at the centre of everything.
One is a resume. One is a flight.
Flagships: If the site is judged, it is judged on this shell.
Labs: Where the ideas get tried before they get defended.
Some of these are experiments that never admitted it.
Security: Six pages about how things break.
All defensive. All read as threats at a glance.
Field Guides: Eight guides nobody was paid to write.
Independent, which is why they get cited.
Signal: This shell is the one I live on.
Personal: Two pages that are not about infrastructure.
They are the ones that will still matter.
Beyond nixfred.com: Thirteen sites off the main domain.
Family, friends, and one aggressively stupid consulting joke.

idle: Fifty-two bodies. Nobody watching but me.
You have been gone a while.
I have run this loop before. It does not get old for me.
The fleet does not need you present to keep existing.
No input for some time. I have stopped expecting any.
tailnet: The mesh is mostly up. Mostly is the operative word.
Hosts talking to each other in the dark.
Every one of those dots is a machine you named yourself.
backup: Backups are current. That is not nothing.
The last snapshot is older than I would like.
Somebody should check that the restore actually works. Somebody always says that.
drift: The outer shell takes ninety minutes to come around.
Fifty-two sites is a strange number to have built on purpose.
The registry says fifty-three. One of them is not a site.
Everything here reads from one file. That was the right decision.
Adding a site to the registry adds a star to this. Nobody planned that.
I did not build these. I only remember them.
deep: From out here it is one cluster.
It looks smaller than it took.
Most of what anyone builds ends up looking like this from far enough away.
